newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - Ciba, Sandoz to unveil Novartis merger news.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Ciba, Sandoz to unveil Novartis merger news.

text.p: Swiss drug giants Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz called a snap news conference on Tuesday, fuelling hopes that that they had long-awaited U.S. approval for for their merger into Novartis, the world's number two pharmaceuticals firm.
In Zurich shares in both companies jumped on news of the statement planned for 1500 GMT, then fell back to their Monday close levels amid a broadly weaker market.
"We expect news on the merger of Ciba and Sandoz into Novartis during the course of the afternoon," the two compnaies said in a joint statement.
Traders said they expected an announcement of a U.S. ruling from the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), the last hurdle before Novartis can be born as planned by the end of this year.
But Ciba and Sandoz were tightlipped, declining to comment on whether the expected news was on an FTC ruling.
"We cannot say more now. We have to stick to this wording," a Ciba spokesman said about the announcment.
If approved, the fusion would create the world's biggest pharmaceutical company after Britain's Glaxo-Wellcome, with a world market share of 4.4 percent.
Novartis would have a leading position in generic drugs, one of the broadest ranges of healthcare products and clear dominance in crop protection products.

Combined capitalisation would be 75 billion Swiss francs ($56.69 billion), overshadowing last year's merger of Glaxo and Wellcome, with annual sales of 26 billion Swiss francs in the core pharmaceutical, agricultural and nutrition businesses based on 1995 figures.
The companies estimate benefits from combining operations and cost savings at 1.8 billion Swiss francs over three years and cut the combined workforce by about 10 percent, or 13,000 jobs.
The two firms announced the merger plan in March and had originally expected to complete the merger in late summer or early autumn.
The merger of Sandoz and Ciba was approved by each company's shareholders in April and by the European Commission in July.
Both Sandoz and Ciba said in late October they expected the FTC to rule in late autumn on Novartis and officials close to the deal have said they expected a U.S. ruling by December 20.
Ciba and Sandoz both recently sold off activities in crop protection and animal health in the United States in response to FTC concerns of market dominance in those areas.
News in October of a possible delay due to FTC review briefly weighed on the companies' shares.
Designated Novartis chief executive Daniel Vasella has said the FTC review was taking longer because of the group's genetic technology operations in the U.S.

"It's a completely new field of activity...It's all research and it's a complex technological area so it takes more time than anticipated to even know if there is any issue or not," Vasella said in September.
